chain.label: FAA flight/duty time rules permitted long demanding day
chain.trigger: Existing FAA pilot flight and duty time regulations permitted the long and demanding day experienced by the accident pilots

chain.label: Captain's check airman OE duties added workload
chain.trigger: the additional responsibilities and task demands involved in providing operating experience and performing related check airman functions likely aggravated the effects of fatigue for the captain/check airman

caused_by.evidence: Federal regulations do not address check airman hours of service apart from general flight and duty time limitations

chain.label: Both pilots fatigued after 14+ hour duty day, awake 16+ hours
chain.trigger: the pilots had flown 8.35 hours, made five landings, been on duty more than 14 hours, and been awake more than 16 hours; CVR recorded numerous yawns and comments that indicate that the pilots were fatigued

caused_by.evidence: existing FAA pilot flight and duty time regulations permitted the long and demanding day...which resulted in their fatigued condition
would have almost certainly exacerbated the development of fatigue for the captain

chain.label: Moderate-to-heavy wet snow contaminated runway 28 after plowing
chain.trigger: moderate-to-heavy snow fell after the snow removal operations were completed, and the runway conditions deteriorated...snow depth had increased to nearly 1/2 inch before the airplane landed

chain.label: TVC snow plan lacked runway-closure criteria for nil braking
chain.trigger: at the time of the accident, TVC's snow and ice control plan did not specify criteria that would result in airport personnel closing a runway and/or the airport

chain.label: Operations supervisor used ambiguous 'probably nil' phraseology and would not confirm nil braking
chain.trigger: the TVC airport operations supervisor's description of 'probably nil'...and his subsequent failure to confirm a nil braking report when questioned further by the pilots likely led the pilots to believe that the runway braking action was not actually nil

caused_by.evidence: he based his nil braking action reports on tests he conducted with his vehicle on runway 28, during which he perceived 'minimal to nonexistent' braking action
If TVC's snow and ice control plan had incorporated such criteria, it is likely that the TVC airport operations supervisor would have...closed the runway to air carrier operations

chain.label: First nil braking report blocked by simultaneous ATC transmission; not heard
chain.trigger: it is likely that neither pilot heard the TVC airport operations supervisor's first nil braking report because that transmission occurred simultaneously with critical approach instructions issued by the controller

caused_by.evidence: the first officer turned down the volume on the TVC CTAF to hear the heading and frequency instructions provided by the controller

chain.label: Crew stopped monitoring ASOS; unaware of deteriorating weather
chain.trigger: the crew monitored the TVC ASOS weather information on only one occasion, about 30 minutes before they landed...They did not obtain a more current observation as they neared the airport

caused_by.evidence: poor decision-making shown by the accident pilots, including their failure to account for the changing weather and runway conditions during the approach...likely reflected the effects of fatigue

chain.label: No arrival landing distance assessment performed as required by OpSpec C382
chain.trigger: The pilots failed to perform the landing distance assessment that was required by Pinnacle's Operations Specifications; had they done so...the results would have shown that the runway length was inadequate

caused_by.evidence: their failure to perform a landing distance calculation...likely reflected the effects of fatigue
he still did not perform a landing distance assessment, which was required for landing with the contamination on the runway
the pilots did not recognize or acknowledge the airport operations supervisor's nil braking action report
the pilots could have made a more informed landing decision if they had monitored the current...TVC weather information

chain.label: No hands-on training on when landing distance assessment is required
chain.trigger: provisions for hands-on training and validation of proficiency were not put into place...neither recognized the need to accomplish this procedure when they were briefed on the contaminated runway conditions

chain.label: Decision to continue approach and land at TVC rather than divert or delay
chain.trigger: the pilots' decision to land at TVC without performing a landing distance assessment, which was required by company policy because of runway contamination

caused_by.evidence: it is likely that fatigue and a desire to end the trip (and their day) influenced the pilots' continuation of the approach despite evidence that they should either delay the approach or divert
the TVC airport operations supervisor's use of ambiguous and unspecific radio phraseology when providing braking action information likely affected the captain's decision to continue the approach
the captain appeared satisfied that the ground cover was within Pinnacle's limitations and continued the approach without performing a landing distance assessment
more thorough training on the rationale behind conducting a landing distance assessment may have made the crew more cognizant of the need for such an assessment

chain.label: Long landing 2,400 ft beyond threshold, past 1,500 ft touchdown zone
chain.trigger: the accident airplane landed farther down the runway than the 1,500-foot touchdown point assumed by the landing distance calculations

caused_by.evidence: the captain announced that the runway was in sight and that they would continue to a landing...touched down on the runway about 2,400 feet from the threshold

chain.label: Insufficient deceleration and left yaw excursion on slippery runway
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's braking ability was more than four times worse than that of a normal dry runway...the airplane heading continued to move nose left, reaching about 25 degrees nose left of the runway heading

caused_by.evidence: typical of a loss of directional stability and rudder effectiveness due to reverser deployment [on a contaminated/slippery runway] at low airspeed in a crosswind from the right

an airplane similarly configured and landing with conditions, touchdown point, and deceleration efforts similar to those of the accident flight would have required an additional 1,146 feet of unobstructed runway to stop

chain.label: Airplane overran departure end of runway 28 at 47 knots, substantial damage
chain.trigger: ran off the departure end of runway 28 after landing at Cherry Capital Airport...at a ground speed of about 47 knots...the aircraft was substantially damaged

caused_by.evidence: The airplane ran off the end of the runway, with thrust reversers stowed, at a ground speed of about 47 knots
